text:
Nora Kim: Quick question
I accepted an internal offer to move teams and my start date on the new team lines up with a pay cycle cutover. I have an active 401(k) loan and an HSA balance. Will my loan repayment and HSA payroll contributions continue uninterrupted during the internal transfer? Any actions I should take?

Ethan Brooks: Congrats on the move! Short answer: usually yes, but depends on payroll org change timing. Loans are plan-level; repayments generally continue, but if your payroll employee ID changes at the cutover there can be a short interruption.

Sam (Benefits Vendor): From the recordkeeper side: we map loans to SSN/employee number. If payroll sends a new employee ID, we reconcile, but there can be a 1-paycycle pause. If your HSA employer code changes, payroll HSA deferrals might stop for that pay.

Nora Kim: Okay. How will I know if a pause happens?

PayrollBot: Automated: "If a loan withholding stops, payroll will open a case and notify the employee within 3 business days. Check your paystub for '401k Loan Repayment' line. For HSA, check the 'Pre-tax Deductions' section."

Ethan Brooks: Action items: 1) Send your transfer HR case number to payroll@redwood.com. 2) Keep an eye on next two paystubs. 3) If repayments stop, we can set up temporary ACH to the recordkeeper on a case-by-case basis to avoid loan default.

Sam (Benefits Vendor): If you're worried about card declines during a swap, note HSA debit card numbers may change only if the recordkeeper or plan sponsor changes. For internal transfers they stay the same.

Nora Kim: Thanks 

One more: I have a pending in-service distribution request (ROTH conversion) submitted last week. Will that process?

Sam (Benefits Vendor): If it was fully approved and transmitted before payroll cutover, it should process. Anything in-flight at cutoff may be delayed; we'll notify you. Email planadmin@vendor.com if you want priority follow-up.

hr-bot: Policy note: "Internal transfers do not change plan eligibility. Payroll ID changes can cause short interruptions to payroll-fed deductions; employees must monitor paystubs and report issues within two pay cycles."

Nora Kim: Perfect 

I sent the HR case and will watch my stub. Thanks team! :thumbsup:
